To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the traditional models of short term memory are insufficient to explain working memory in text comprehension, and that the proposed framework of long term working memory based on retrieval cues provides a promising account for working memory in skilled activities.
the memory demands on text comprehension and expert problem solving are very high and that the traditional working memory model is too limited in its capacity to account for these demands.

the capacity and duration of working memory is not limited by the number of items in short term memory and that the capacity and durability of working memory is limited by the amount of knowledge that is directly accessible in long term memory, and that this knowledge is organized in a hierarchical fashion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of long term memory in skilled performance, and the role of working memory in the development of skilled performance.
the nature of the long term working memory, and how it supports the cognitive processing of information in skilled activities.
the development of models of human information processing and memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the traditional models of memory are inadequate to account for the large working memory demands during text comprehension and skilled performance.
long term working memory is a necessary component in any model of working memory.
the traditional models of short term memory are inadequate for explaining memory phenomena in text comprehension and expertise, and that a model of long term working memory is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed theoretical framework can account for the large memory demands of skilled performance.
long-term working memory is a key factor in text comprehension and in expert performance.

the traditional view of working memory as temporary storage is not sufficient to explain long term working memory in text comprehension, and that long term working memory is an important factor in expert performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
long term working memory, based on storage in memory and retrieval from long term memory, is an essential component of working memory.
the working memory capacity of an expert is not fixed and can be extended through the use of long term memory.
working memory is not just a short term store but rather a long term store of stable states.
